items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: I never will forget one night at Manhattan Center... place packed and jammed with all the biggest bands in New York City -- Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, Benny Goodman, just all of them.

ctx.x: I mean in terms of the audiences. Were the audiences basically the same. I mean the way they acted.

Well, they were colored, Naturally, they were swingers. Whites were jitterbugging, you know, that kind of thing. I never will forget one night at Manhattan Center. I have (inaudible). We played at a ball. It was just a ball, place packed and jammed with all the biggest bands in New York City -- Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, Benny Goodman, just all of them.

Each band was supposed to go on the stand and play for 15 minutes only, no more, no less. Lunceford's band got on that stand, and if I must say myself (inaudible) bunch with us dancing, jitterbugs like [Shoe Birch] and all that bunch. We got up there, and we couldn't get off. That band was exciting, throwing the trumpets in there and catching them, trombones sliding and then catch it with the left hand. I don't know how they did it.
